p.t: In short
p.s: Platform choice, Shopify plan, trial and account setup

p.t: Use **Shopify** for every store. It is one ready-made platform (software you rent to run a shop) that does almost everything.
Start on the **Basic** plan. Higher plans only make sense when sales are large or the team is big.
Start the **free trial before you choose a plan. Cancel before the trial ends** so you are not charged.
Use **one Shopify account per store**. Build the store directly on Shopify, not somewhere else.
Prices, trial offers and plan limits change often. Check them on the Shopify checkout page before you rely on them.
**Wait** to open the Shopify account (online store software) until you start building the website, because the free trial starts at signup.
Use a **business email if you have one. A personal email such as Gmail also works. Confirm the verification email within about 24 hours**.

Give helpers a **staff account or collaborator** access, never your main login.
Pay **monthly** while the store is unproven, and do not sign a long contract at the start.
Do not build a full store until the product gets views and is close to **1,000** TikTok followers.
Why Shopify
p.s: Platform choice, Shopify plan, trial and account setup

p.t: **Shopify** is the platform this handbook uses for every store. A platform is the ready-made software that runs a store.
Shopify is built only for e-commerce, which means selling products online.
Shopify covers these jobs in one place: domain setup (your web address), storefront design (what customers see), product management, inventory tracking (counting stock),
payment processing (taking payments), checkout (the final buying step), analytics (sales statistics), email marketing, live chat, and built-in connections to the Google
and Facebook sales channels (places where you sell).
Shopify's all-in-one scope means **no separate tools** are needed for store design, product management, payments, inventory, email, order tracking, live chat or analytics.
Shopify is the recommended **primary platform** (the main one) for dropshipping. Dropshipping means a supplier ships each product straight to the customer, so you do not keep stock.
Shopify has superior integrations (connections to other tools) and technology built for e-commerce fulfillment (packing and shipping orders).
Shopify allows **unlimited** product uploads on day one.
Shopify is recommended for dropshipping stores because of its supplier-friendly integrations and app ecosystem. Apps are add-on tools, and the ecosystem is the full range of them.
Other site builders are not recommended for stores that will run paid ads (paid advertising).
Shopify was chosen over newer website builders for its maturity (being well established) and its feature depth (how many useful functions it has).
The newer alternatives were considered too young for a serious store at the time of the source.
The course recommends Shopify as the **single platform** for every store.
Shopify is described as the market leader (the biggest seller in its field) for about ten years, with the best platform and support.
Using one account for all tools is preferred over combining several tools.
Shopify is a managed platform. The merchant (you, the store owner) does **not host** (keep on servers), secure or maintain the software.

Shopify has rarely been down for stores.
Custom setups add hosting latency (delay from servers) and maintenance work.
Why Shopify (continued)
p.s: Platform choice, Shopify plan, trial and account setup

p.t: A custom build (a site coded from scratch) would need separate APIs (connection points between software), such as PayPal and Stripe (payment services).
Those APIs would be needed to copy the checkout, supplier connections and order back end (the hidden system that handles orders) that Shopify already includes.
Shopify handles the frontend (the storefront customers see) and the backend (the back office that runs ordering, checkout, and product and order management).
You work in the backend every day. Customers only see the frontend.
A hosted platform already includes ordering, checkout, order management and product management. A beginner only adds design and content.
This avoids a custom website, which typically costs **tens of thousands of dollars**.

A first business should not begin with a large upfront website development cost (money paid before launch).
That money is hard to recover if the business fails.
The priority is to **launch quickly** on a platform that is easy to use.
Shopify is recommended for beginners because it combines ease of use, easy daily management and cost-effectiveness (good value for money).
BigCommerce, Magento, WooCommerce and WordPress can also work, but they are harder for newcomers.
An experienced builder can use another platform if they already know it well.
Shopify is used to build an online store in **minutes or hours** without coding (writing software code) or web development knowledge. It uses free themes (ready-made page designs) and apps.

The build is done step by step and does not require prior website experience.
Shopify is for beginners with little or no coding experience.
Shopify is mobile responsive, which means it adjusts to phone screens.
Shopify handles security topics such as data encryption (scrambling data so others cannot read it).
Shopify also handles fraud prevention (stopping fake orders) and PCI compliance (meeting the card industry's security rules).
Shopify can be used for both physical products and digital products (files or access sold online).
**Full-time support** is available by chat, plus an active community (other users who help each other).
Why Shopify (continued)
p.s: Platform choice, Shopify plan, trial and account setup

p.t: Answers to most common questions can be found through Google or the Shopify support pages.
Large consumer brands such as Kylie Cosmetics, Tesla Motors and Gym Shark run their e-commerce on Shopify. This shows the platform works at very large scale.

Many of the largest e-commerce stores still run on Shopify.
A store can grow on Shopify for a long time before a platform change is needed.
Shopify is suited to beginners starting a new business from scratch.
Shopify is the platform used to build the high-ticket store in this course. High-ticket means selling expensive products.

The coaching team supports only Shopify stores and does not work with WooCommerce.
Feedback on a non-Shopify site will be limited.

Build the store **directly on Shopify**, not elsewhere and then imported.
Imported stores often need a lot of rework.
A Shopify store stays on the Shopify platform.
Moving to another e-commerce platform later requires an app-based migration (moving the store with an app) and substantial rework.
Moving a Shopify store to a self-hosted platform (one you run on your own servers) is not seamless.
A developer can model the existing store on a new platform, since Shopify's structure is well established and widely understood.
Shopify takes a percentage of each sale (a transaction fee), so the platform's cost depends on sales volume. See the plan section below.
Shopify is a managed platform that is recommended over self-hosted alternatives. Self-hosted alternatives require the merchant to handle hosting, security and customer data protection.
Marketplaces such as eBay and Facebook Marketplace bring organic traffic (free visitors, not paid ones).
Users on marketplaces visit with purchase intent (they are ready to buy).
Google search traffic requires strong SEO (search engine optimisation, getting found in Google results) or paid ads.
Shopify has harder initial traffic acquisition (getting visitors at the start).
Shopify enables better long-term retargeting (showing ads again to people who already visited) and scaling (growing sales).
Alternatives and when they fit
p.s: Platform choice, Shopify plan, trial and account setup

p.t:
WooCommerce is self-hosted and needs separate hosting and plug-ins (add-on tools).
Shopify keeps hosting, security and support in **one platform**.

WooCommerce plug-ins and add-ons are often paid.
Compare the total add-on cost with Shopify before choosing WooCommerce.

WooCommerce is **not recommended** for dropshipping.
Magento only makes sense for stores with around **50,000 to 100,000 or more products**.

Do not mix WordPress and Shopify for new stores.
Shopify's blogging system (the part for writing articles) and SEO capabilities are excellent.
Combine WordPress with Shopify only if you already own an established WordPress site with significant history and traffic, such as a blog subdomain (a section of a site with its own address).

Use WordPress for standalone blogs or review sites that earn affiliate commissions (money from partner links).
Use Shopify for stores that sell products directly.
WordPress and BigCommerce are alternatives with similar ecosystems to Shopify.
ClickFunnels creates single-page checkout funnels (a short page path that leads to a purchase).
Shopify product pages achieve the same conversion goals (getting visitors to buy) at **lower cost**, with better e-commerce integrations.
Shopify is preferred for dropshipping because it was designed for e-commerce fulfillment, not generic funnel building.

Shopify is the only store platform used for these stores.
Funnel builders such as ClickFunnels are not used in place of Shopify.
Shopify gives the seller another sales channel. It lets them send traffic from Google and Bing to their own products.
A separate store also avoids losing buyers to other products on Amazon, because visitors who land on Amazon often buy something else.
A Shopify store makes retargeting, upsells (extra offers after a purchase) and email capture (collecting email addresses) easier than Amazon does.
A Shopify store keeps the focus on your own products, which is hard to do with Amazon's search results.
Compare the conversion rate (the share of visitors who buy) of a digital product on Shopify with PayHip (a platform for selling digital products) before choosing a platform.

Test both with the same offer to see which converts better.
PayHip allows PayPal and Stripe to be connected. These are the two most important payment options for digital products.
Check the platform fee per purchase before choosing PayHip, since the fee is not stated here.
Moving an existing Wix store to Shopify
p.s: Platform choice, Shopify plan, trial and account setup

p.t: Wix is another website builder.
Move from Wix to Shopify for an e-commerce store, because Shopify is built only for e-commerce and has more apps and built-in tools.

Keep existing logos, images and written content when migrating.
Migration procedure :
1. Look for a dedicated importer app (a tool that moves data into Shopify). **None was found** for Wix at the time of the source.

2. Export the products from Wix as a CSV file (a spreadsheet file).
3. Import the CSV into Shopify.
4. Recreate the collections (product groups), pages and text manually in Shopify.

p.t:
The Basic plan is the one used for most new stores.
**Monthly price across sources (conflicting figures).**

Basic at **USD 29 per month** was the figure in 2020 and 2021 sources.
In 2020, Basic was described as the recommended tier (plan level) for most stores.
In 2020, Basic was also described as enough functionality for about 99% of stores.
(2023.) Basic was **29 USD per month when paid for a year in advance, or 39 USD per month** when paid monthly.
(2026.) Basic is listed at about **USD 39 per month** plus tax after the introductory period.
One source gives about 79 USD per month for Basic and almost 300 USD per month for Advanced.

The 2021 table lists 79 USD for the middle Shopify tier and 29 USD for Basic.
The two sources disagree. Verify on the current plan page.
**Shopify Plus thresholds (conflicting figures; each applies to a different claim).** Shopify Plus is the top enterprise plan (for very large stores).
Upgrade to Plus only if processing fee savings (money saved on card-handling fees) exceed a minimum of **5,000 USD per month**.

(2024.) Custom Checkout (your own checkout design) is available only on the **2,300 USD per month** Plus plan.
Standard plans do not include custom checkout.

Full control over checkout design and costs requires Plus, which costs at least **2,000 USD per month**.
This makes Plus unsuitable for most new stores.
Checkout apps that inject code (insert extra software into the checkout) are fragile and often stop working over time.
Plus only makes sense for stores at **nine-figure revenue** (at least 100 million USD a year) or mid eight-figure revenue (tens of millions of USD a year).

Below that level, Plus is not worth the extra cost.
Verify the current Plus price and the revenue condition before deciding.

The sources in this set do not agree on the minimum.
**Plan restrictions that change the choice.**
The Shopify 39 USD per month plan does **not include staff accounts** (logins for employees).
Agencies or partners use a collaborator invitation (a way for outside helpers to get access) instead. Partner access does not require a staff account.
The Basic plan changed on **24 January** without notice. It can only sell in free markets (countries without extra limits) and cannot run multi-market setups (selling in several countries).
Check plan limits regularly, because a plan change can break an existing store configuration.
Choosing and switching a plan
p.s: Platform choice, Shopify plan, trial and account setup

p.t: Start a new Shopify store on the **Basic plan**, not on Shopify or Advanced Shopify.
Higher plans are worth it only once a store has more staff or a large volume of sales.

The switch point to a higher plan is approximately **30,000 to 40,000 USD monthly revenue** (money from sales each month).
Verify this against current pricing.
Higher plans charge a lower transaction percentage per sale.
A higher plan such as Advanced can pay off at high monthly sales, because the lower percentage adds up across many orders.
On Shopify Advanced, the transaction percentage was about **1 percentage point lower** (1 full percent) than on the plan below it.

Advanced was cheaper when billed yearly rather than monthly.
Billing yearly was cheaper than monthly for Advanced.

Shopify offers a discounted annual (yearly) price when paying up front.
Committing to a multi-year term is not advisable at the start.
Monthly billing keeps the cost flexible while the store is unproven.
The annual option can be considered once the store's sales and staffing needs are clear.

A plan upgrade can come with a temporary free period (a promotion), such as three free months on Shopify Advanced.
After it ends, the store may revert to Basic without notice.
**Note the expiry date**, because a reversion can cancel multi-market settings that depend on the higher plan.

Verification rules
p.s: Platform choice, Shopify plan, trial and account setup

p.t:
Confirm the trial terms before you rely on them.
Promotions change, and the same offer may not be shown to everyone.
Check the current price and offer on the Shopify checkout page before subscribing.
Promotional offers reached through a referral or affiliate link (a link from someone who invited you or earns from your sign-up) can differ from the public offer.
Compare the price on the official Shopify site **before paying** for a plan.
The 3-month-for-1-USD offer was not shown to everyone. It appeared to depend on the user's IP address (a number that identifies your internet connection).
To claim it, open the link and **create the account right away**, because the offer can disappear once the IP is recognised.

The trial shows at the top of the new Shopify admin (the back office).
The store must be on a paid plan before launching.

If a trial has ended, a trial extension can be requested from Shopify support.
A trial extension gives **14 additional days**.
Support may refuse if the offer is only for qualifying participants.
Each new account can ask Shopify support for an extra two weeks, extending a 14-day trial to **28 days**.

This can be done regardless of how far into the trial the account is.
Reported in 2022: several stores under one account may each get a 14-day trial.
Verify this in Shopify **before relying on it**.
The plan selection screen allows a plan to be cancelled before the trial ends **without any charge**.

Choose the plan and note the trial end date so that a cancellation can be made in time.
Remaining free trial days are kept before the first payment.
Forgetting to cancel before a free trial ends results in the **full monthly plan price** being charged.
The checkout states the cancellation deadline, so note the date when you sign up.
One account per store
p.s: Platform choice, Shopify plan, trial and account setup

p.t: Each separate store needs its own Shopify account and bill.

A single Google account can manage several stores, but keep them separate to make a later sale of one store easier.
Each Shopify store needs its own Shopify account.
An unused second account should be cancelled to avoid paying for it.
One Shopify account equals one store, regardless of the plan. A single account cannot host several separate niche stores.
Each separate store needs its own account, because one account supports one store.
The name chosen at signup becomes the permanent myshopify.com address (Shopify's own default web address) to which custom domains are attached.

Each new store requires a new account.
The same email address can be used to switch between accounts after logging in.
Several accounts can share one login email using single sign-on (one login that opens several accounts).

One merchant account number cannot be used across several websites.
Related stores can share a legal entity (a registered company).

Each unrelated group of stores should get its own legal entity.
Use a **new email address for each new Shopify account** to keep stores organised.

When creating a new account, use an email address that is the same as or closely similar to the TikTok account's email.
This makes it easy to match each store to its accounts.
The sources differ on whether one login can manage several stores.
The Google login and single sign-on statements allow several accounts under one login. The one-account-per-store statements keep each store separate.
Keep **one account per store**, and verify trial counts in Shopify before relying on them.

p.t: Two positions appear in the set. Use the one that fits your stage.
Do not open the Shopify account early. Open it when you start building the website, because early setup mistakes must otherwise be fixed later.
The **14-day** free trial (a free test period) is wasted if it runs before the build.
The **14-day** free trial starts at signup, so do not open the account before the website build stage.
Opening the account before the website stage starts the trial too early. Early setup mistakes must then be fixed.
**Wait** until the store build step, when you have a verified market (a market you have checked) and are ready to build.
Do not **activate** the Shopify plan (monthly package) before you build the store.
Confirm the first two stages are fully completed before using the Shopify extended trial link (a special signup link with a longer free trial).
A Shopify account is required whether you build the demo store (a sample store) yourself or the done-for-you team builds it. So create it first.

Business email and signup details
p.s: Platform choice, Shopify plan, trial and account setup

p.t: **Email address**
Use a **business email address** for the Shopify account and all business communication, not a personal inbox.
The verification email (the confirmation message Shopify sends) must be opened and confirmed within about **24 hours**.
A personal email address can be used, including one from a personal account, because it can be changed later.

A business email is not required. A regular personal email such as Gmail works.
On the sign-up page, type the business email address into the **Email address** field.

**Verification**
If the verification email does not arrive, find the **Verify your email address** card on the dashboard (the home screen).

Click **Resend verification email** to get the confirmation link sent again.
This keeps the account verifiable within the **24-hour** window.

**Business details**
The business entity name (the legal company name) does not need to match your domain name (your web address) or brand.
Simple names such as ER Stores LLC or Online Stores LLC are acceptable.

The entity name appears on bank accounts and tax documents. The domain is your public-facing store name.
A **US address** is not required to open a Shopify account.
A US address is optional for business setup. A virtual or physical US address can be added later if needed. (2024.)
If you have no company yet, pick your home country as the business location (for example, the United States, or the country you live in).
Onboarding (the first setup screens), Step 2 of 2, is titled **Add an address so you can get paid**.
Its fields are First name, Last name, Address, Suburb, Country/Region, Phone, State/territory, Postcode and the optional Business or personal website.
Below them is a checkbox labelled **This store is a registered business**, followed by the **Enter my store** button.
Business email and signup details (continued)

p.t:
Onboarding Step 1 of 2 offers sales-channel choices (the places you sell).
Under Online Store: Online Store, Social media and Online marketplaces.
Under In person: At markets and fairs, At pop-ups and In brick and mortar retail stores.
Selecting any in-person option leads to point-of-sale offers (offers for in-store payment tools).

The question Are you setting up a store for a client? is for agencies (firms that build stores for others).
A solo online-only merchant should select only **Online Store**.

**Signup procedures (each source kept in full)**
Procedure A, Source D 2026:
1. Enter your email on the sign-up page and click **Next**.

2. Enter a password.
3. Choose the **Basic plan in the plan selection and click Try basic**.

4. In the checkout (the payment page), check the trial end, the renewal date (the day the next charge starts), the plan price (about $39/month plus tax) and the introductory $1/month rate (a discounted first price).

Then click **Subscribe**.
5. Dismiss the upsell offer (an extra sales offer) with **Not now**.
6. On the 'What can we help you do?' screen, select **Sell online and Dropshipping (selling products that a supplier ships to the customer), then click Continue**.

7. Enter a store name (the default is 'My Store' and can be changed later) and click **Continue**, or choose **I'll do this later**.
Procedure B, Source C:

1. Go to shopify.com, enter your email address and click 'Start free trial'.
2. A business email is not required. A regular personal email such as Gmail works.
3. On the first question, choose 'I'm just starting an online store' and select dropshipping products as the product type.
4. If you have no company yet, pick your home country as the business location (for example, United States, or the country you live in) and click **Next**.
5. Choose 'Continue with email', set a password and click 'Create Shopify ID' (your Shopify login).
6. Once the account exists, open the settings options and fill in the business details: store name, time zone and main currency.
Business email and signup details (continued)

p.t: 7. Under Domains you can buy a custom domain, which becomes the professional domain later.
8. If sign-up asks for a domain name, Shopify provides a default one ending in.myshopify.com (Shopify's free built-in web address).
9. Any name works, because this default domain is **not used for promotion**.
10. Open the **Online Store section and then Themes** (store design templates), where Shopify's free themes can be selected.

1. Open the Shopify extended trial offer link provided with this guide.
2. Create a Shopify account through that page: **3 days free, then the first three months at $1 per month**.
3. Enter any email address, personal ones included, since it can be changed later.
4. After the account is set up, either continue building the demo store yourself or submit the done-for-you web design form (a request for someone else to build the store).

Procedure D, Source A step order:
1. Confirm the first two stages are fully completed.
2. Use the Shopify extended trial link to create your account.
3. Decide whether to build yourself or use the Done-For-You service (someone else builds the store for you).

4. If using Done-For-You, submit the web design form.
5. If building yourself, proceed to the next step.
6. Mark this step complete.

Procedure E, Source B sign-up page:
Open the Shopify sign-up page and type the business email address into the **Email address** field.

The name chosen at signup becomes the permanent myshopify.com address (Shopify's built-in web address).

Custom domains are attached to that myshopify.com address.

Admin orientation
p.s: Platform choice, Shopify plan, trial and account setup

p.t: The Shopify **admin** (the back-end control panel that customers do not see) is where the store is managed.
In the admin you manage storefront design, product upload, product page design and inventory tracking (stock counts).
The front end (what customers see) of the store is designed inside this admin.
The left-hand navigation contains Home, Orders, Products, Customers, Analytics, Marketing, Discounts, Apps, Sales channels, Online Store and Settings at the bottom.

**Orders and products are managed daily** here.
Analytics (sales and visitor reports) and sales data start to fill in only after the store goes live.
Until the store is launched, the storefront is protected by a **password**, so the public cannot see it.
A new store shows only a basic home page with no design or images until the **theme** (store design template) is customised.

Practise Shopify edits on the free trial, which was **14 to 21 days** at the time this was written.
You can also practise on a copy of a store in progress.
This prevents accidental deletions from damaging the live store.
The dashboard card titled **Your trial just started** lists four first setup tasks: Add your first product, Customize theme, Add domain and Set up payments.
Working through these four items in that order gives a new store its basic setup after account creation.
The Shopify admin home page shows a setup checklist for a new store with Add product, Customize theme, Add domain and Set up payments.
Admin orientation (continued)
p.s: Platform choice, Shopify plan, trial and account setup

p.t:
These mark the main steps before launch.
Initial setup checklist on the Shopify admin Home page, in this order:
1. Add store name.

2. Discover products to sell: install a recommended supplier app or add a product manually.
3. Set up Shopify Payments (Shopify's built-in payment service): click **Activate**.

4. Customize your online store: choose or generate a theme, then add logo, colors and images.
5. Review your shipping rates.
6. Customize domain: the store starts on a default myshopify.com address and a custom domain can be added.
**Settings > Plan** shows the current plan, the trial terms (in the example, 3 months at $1 per month), the date monthly billing starts, and the payment method.

Plan changes and switching to **annual billing** are made on this page.
**Settings > Billing** shows the stored payment method and billing currency.

It also shows active subscriptions, including paid apps with their next bill, and previous charges.
Use it to track what is paid to Shopify.

**Settings > Users** shows who has access.
The Pending tab shows requests from the agency.

Shopify login problems can come from being logged into a different Shopify account.
Use the admin URL (yourstore.com/admin) to log in to the correct store.

Or try an incognito window (a private browser window) or a different browser. (2025.)
To **deactivate** (switch off) a Shopify store you created by mistake:

1. Open the Shopify admin.
2. Click **Settings**.
3. Open **Plan**.
4. Click **Deactivate**.
Shopify may put the store on hold for a while in case you change your mind.
Collaborator and staff accounts
p.s: Platform choice, Shopify plan, trial and account setup

p.t:
**Staff accounts**
Shopify **Staff Accounts** let the store owner give team members limited access to the store.

This means they get access without sharing the main login.
Create staff accounts for contractors and designers.
Set **permissions** (rules for what each person may open) to restrict access to customer data, payment settings and financial information.

Each staff member can have different permission levels.
When bringing in a VA (virtual assistant, a remote helper), use staff permissions.
Give them only the access they need, such as editing store pages. Keep financial or other sensitive areas closed.

Permissions to grant: Products, Catalogs (product lists), Online store and Store settings.
**Do not grant** access to Orders, Draft orders (unfinished orders) or Customers. (2024.)
Settings > Users and permissions > Add staff: invite a person (for example, a hired store builder) by name and email.

Then choose which sections of the store they can access.
This gives them a separate login instead of sharing your username and password.
**Collaborator accounts**

Shopify collaborator accounts give a staff member or outside partner access to a store.
Use them **instead of sharing credentials** (login details).

The collaborator request arrives by email once assets are ready (the store files are finished).
For agencies or partners on the 39 USD per month plan, use a collaborator invitation.
Partner access does not require a staff account.
Give a private supplier access by going to shopify.partners and inviting them as a partner (an outside business with its own access).

Grant them partnership access to your Shopify store.
The supplier provides the step-by-step instructions. This guide does not name the exact menu labels.
Cost of running the store
p.s: Platform choice, Shopify plan, trial and account setup

p.t:
**Fixed costs**
Shopify is a **fixed cost** (the same amount every month) that must be paid every month while the store is running.

Stopping payment can lead to the store being shut down.
Shopify costs **29 USD** per month when paid for a year in advance.
Shopify costs **39 USD** per month when paid monthly. (2023.)
The Shopify subscription at 29 USD per month is small compared with the cost of a physical retail store.
A physical store needs a lease (a rental contract), a rent deposit, build-out (interior construction) and fixtures (shelves and fittings).

A store that makes only one **1,000 USD** sale per month still covers the subscription cost.
Shopify costs in the 2021 setting: a **14-day free trial, then 29 USD** per month.

Startup costs before launch
**Domain name**
Cost: $5 to $20
Notes: one-off
**Shopify**

Cost: 14-day free trial, then $29 per month
Notes: do not activate before you build
**Branding and logo on Fiverr**

Cost: about $20 to $30
Notes: logo and branding
**Total to launch**
Cost: about $100
Notes: time not counted
A premium Shopify theme (a paid store design template) can sell for around **$300** when bought separately.
Stores are built on a theme that handles the background code (the hidden instructions that make the store work).

A hosted platform (a ready-made website service) avoids the cost and time of a custom website.
A custom website typically runs to **tens of thousands of dollars**.

A domain name cost about **14 USD per year**.
**Transaction and add-on costs**
A transaction fee is the cut taken from each sale.
Cost of running the store (continued)
p.s: Platform choice, Shopify plan, trial and account setup

p.t: Transaction fees per sale by plan are listed in the plans section: Basic 2.0%, Shopify 1.0%, Advanced 0.5% in the 2021 source.

Add-ons are extra paid features.
Add-on prices: POS Pro (in-store sales software) USD 89/month per location; Remove online store USD 9/month.
Paid apps (add-on tools) appear on the Billing page with their next bill.

For plans that cost more, **Advanced was cheaper when billed yearly** rather than monthly.
**Keeping the cost under control**

Do not commit to a **multi-year term** (a long contract) at the start.
Pay monthly while the store is unproven.

Note the expiry date of any free period.
A reversion (a return to the normal price) may cancel multi-market settings (settings for selling in several countries).

Cancel any unused second account to avoid paying for it.
Check plan limits regularly, since a plan change can break an existing store configuration (the store setup).
Shopify is the platform (the software base) used to build the online store.

A ready-made Shopify theme is used during the store build stage.
Shopify is an ecommerce platform (software for building online stores).

Signing up through a dedicated trial link can give an extended free trial period instead of the standard one.
All stores in this model are built on the Shopify platform.

Shopify is used to design the store, upload products, and manage orders.
Shopify offers a **14-day** free trial before the monthly fee starts.

Shopify is the e-commerce platform recommended for building the dropshipping store.
A Shopify free trial is the starting point for building a new store.

It can be used to test the platform before paying for a plan.
Store content pages can be built faster with ready-made content page templates.
